rationale: DARTGAP1's real missing edge. The pattern-binding QUESTION was already settled by measurement (a pattern-bound name is a binding, not a symbol: reads publish `uses` with the family's `<callable>\u0000<binding>` spelling and `localBinding`, exactly like a parameter), so that half needs no new emission. What was genuinely missing is `rest_pattern`: the grammar spells `...rest` as `(rest_pattern (constant_pattern (identifier)))` (probed in pattern-forms-probe.ts) and `collectDartLocals` never collected it, so `rest` was not in `locals` and every later read of it fell through every read arm and published NOTHING. The fix collects the rest name; the read then takes the ordinary binding arm. The record-pattern and object-pattern cases pin the convention the fix must not disturb, and the forbids pin the other direction: a pattern identifier is a BINDING, never a constant test, so no bare `uses` row for any of these names may appear.

expectRelationships.note: CONVENTION REGRESSION — a destructuring binding's read: `first` comes from `variable_pattern`, which was already collected. Kept here so the rest fix cannot narrow the existing binding surface.

THE NEW EDGE — `...rest`'s read. Before the fix this row did not exist at all: `rest` was absent from `locals`, so `print(rest.length)` published only the member read of `length` and nothing for the binding itself.
CONVENTION REGRESSION — a for-in record-pattern binding's read (`(int p, int q)`), already covered by variable_pattern.
the second binding of the same for-in.
CONVENTION REGRESSION — an object-pattern binding's read (`String(length: final len)`), already covered by variable_pattern.

forbidRelationships.note: A PATTERN BINDING IS NEVER A BARE READ — the binding spelling is what keeps the store from binding it to an unrelated declaration (validation/m14/fixtures/dart/local-read-phantom.ts is the counterfactual for the whole convention).
the same rule for the rest element, in the direction the fix could have broken: treating `...rest` as a constant TEST would publish a bare read of the name being bound.
the same for a record-pattern binding.
the same for an object-pattern binding.
